scenarios.context: A student reports a lost backpack.

speakerA.en: Lost property office. How can I help you?
Can you describe it, please?
What was inside it?
What time did you get off the bus?
I see a blue backpack here, handed in by the driver. Could you tell me your name and address?
Good, that matches the name in the notebook. You can collect it today until six.

speakerB.en: Hello. I think I left my backpack on the number twelve bus about an hour ago.
It's dark blue with a red zip, and it has a small football badge.
My school books, a pencil case and a water bottle. There's also a notebook with my name on it.
At about half past three, near the library.
Of course. It's Arash Karimi, and my address is 25 Garden Street.
Thank you so much. I'll come right away with my father.

scenarios.scenario: A problem in a group project
scenarios.context: Two classmates talk honestly about sharing the work.

speakerA.en: Can we talk about the project? I feel I'm doing most of the work.
I understand, but the deadline is on Friday, and we still haven't finished the slides.
Could you finish the research part by Wednesday?
Put it in the shared file so Nima and Sara can see it too.
Good idea. I'll ask the others if they can come after school.
Thanks for being honest and understanding.

speakerB.en: You're right. I'm sorry. I've been busy with football.
What can I do to help? I want to fix this.
Yes, I can do it tomorrow evening. Should I send it to you or put it in our shared file?
Okay. And let's meet on Thursday to practise the presentation.
If they can't, we can practise online in the evening.
No problem. We're a team, so let's make it work.

scenarios.context: A daughter and her father discuss which school to choose.

speakerA.en: Dad, I have to choose a school for next year, and I'm confused.
I like science, but I also love drawing. I don't know which is more important.
That one is good, but it's far away. I'd have to take two buses.
The closer school has a smaller science programme, but a very good art club.
That sounds like a good compromise. Can we visit it on Saturday?
Thanks, Dad. I feel much better about the decision now.

speakerB.en: Let's look at the options together. What are you interested in?
Many schools offer both. What about the school near the university?
That's true. It would take almost an hour each way.
Then you could study science there and join the club for your drawing.
Yes, they have an open day. We can meet the teachers and ask questions.
Take your time. It's your future, and you'll make a good choice.

scenarios.context: A customer talks to a shop assistant about a problem.

speakerA.en: Hello. I bought these headphones here last week, but one side doesn't work.
Yes, here it is. I also kept the box.
Can I get my money back?
I'd like a new pair, because I like this model.
Black, please. If it's not available, I'll take a refund.
That's great. Could I test it before I leave?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt?
Thank you. Let me check. You bought them on the sixth, so they're still under warranty.
We can offer you a new pair or a refund. Which would you prefer?
Of course. Let me check if we have one in the same colour.
You're lucky. We have one left. I'll bring it in a minute.
Certainly. You can connect it to the phone on the counter and try it.

scenarios.context: A boy asks his friend for advice about a broken window.

speakerA.en: I need your advice. I broke my neighbour's window with a ball, and nobody saw.
Part of me wants to say nothing. I'm afraid he'll be angry.
I'd want the person to tell me the truth.
You're right. But what if he asks me to pay for it?
That's a good idea. I could water his garden or wash his car.
Okay, I'll go and talk to him this evening.

speakerB.en: Oh dear. What are you thinking of doing?
I understand, but think about how you'd feel if you were him.
Exactly. Lying could also make things worse if he finds out later.
You could offer to help with the cost by doing small jobs for him.
I think he'd appreciate your honesty. Most people forgive honest mistakes.
Good for you. Do you want me to come with you for support?
